audit.whatIsWrong: The early-game paragraph claims Swain 'has no ranged poke besides landing that root' and is left 'auto-attacking into your longer range'.
audit.why: Death's Hand is a 750-range piercing poke on 7/6/5/4/3s that ramps with each bolt hit. He absolutely pokes; what he lacks is a way to close. The real edge is 900 Pillar and 1050 Sear against his 750.
audit.corrected: early rewritten around the actual range war and Nevermove's readable travel-and-return.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4] (Level 6) is rated for Brand with the why 'Lane all-ins favor the arsonist', while win[4] and the packet chart both give level 6 to Swain and whys[4] explains why.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension is a flat 120s, 650 radius, and lasts as long as he keeps draining a champion — the one stage of this lane he owns outright.
audit.corrected: Flagged in notes rather than half-edited (see the chart note); cooldowns and dosFull[0].d now state the radius and the duration rule.

audit.why: Brand's only stun is Sear (Q) against an already-ablaze target; Pillar of Flame (W) is a delayed 900-range AoE that adds 25% damage to ablaze units.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text, early, wants.you[0] rewritten onto the Conflagration-into-Sear package.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain mode — disengage and reset the fight when it starts. It governs your forward steps. - E-Q stun package spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Swain Demonic Ascension: a flat 120s, 650 radius, and it lasts as long as he keeps draining someone — leave the radius, don't out-trade it. Nevermove is 12s at rank 1 and Death's Hand only 3s at rank 5. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.

edits.before: Carry through AoE math — no burst mage damages three targets like Brand; your job is the spacing that lets the bounces vote.
edits.after: Carry through AoE math — Swain's drain pays him for every body in 650 range, so fight him spread out and let the bounces count.

edits.before: His drain mode — disengage and reset the fight when it starts. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension has a 650 radius and heals off everything in it — step out of the circle instead of trading inside it.

edits.before: E the instant ablaze, Q the stun, W the stunned body, walk — the full package chunks half a bar and the burn writes the receipt.
edits.after: Conflagration is point-and-click at 625 range, so the ablaze lands even when Nevermove's root is the thing he is waiting on.

edits.before: Swain whiffs Demonic Ascension and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Swain drops out of Demonic Ascension — 120 seconds are yours.

edits.before: That is Swain’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Death's Hand is back every 3 seconds — your Sear is not.

edits.before: W-poking on cooldown with Q unbanked while his engage is loaded — Brand without the stun threat is a bonfire waiting for company.
edits.after: Ravenous Flock heals him off every unit he hits and permanently raises his max health — anti-heal beats out-damaging that.

edits.before: Your Pillar of Flame stun punishes Swain's slow Vision of Empire/Nevermove cast animation, letting you land a full combo before he can even root you back.
edits.after: Conflagration for the ablaze into a Sear stun punishes Nevermove's slow travel-and-return, letting you land a full combo before the root ever connects.

edits.before: Swain's root has decent range but a very telegraphed windup, and your Pillar of Flame stun comes out faster, so if you play with good spacing you can consistently stun him first and land a full combo before his root ever connects. He has no ranged poke besides landing that root, so if you deny it entirely he's stuck auto-attacking into your longer range with nothing to show for it. Keep pressuring his mana and HP through levels 1-2 so he never gets a comfortable base timer.
edits.after: Nevermove travels out and roots on the way back at 850 range, so it is readable, and an ablaze target plus Sear stuns him first if you hold your spacing and land a full combo before the root connects. Death's Hand still pokes 750 units on a 7-second cooldown, so deny the root and win the range war at 900 and 1050 instead of standing at his. Keep pressuring his mana and HP through levels 1-2 so he never gets a comfortable base timer.

edits.before: Stun him with Pillar before he can land Nevermove root back
edits.after: Stun him with an ablaze Sear before Nevermove roots you
